Field.name: InputFile
Field.usage: Input file with volume to be reduced and/or filtered

Field.name: OutputFile
Field.usage: Output file for reduced and/or filtered volume

Field.name: ReductionFactor
Field.tooltip: Factor to reduce by in X and Y, and in Z if separate factor for Z is not entered. Can be non-integer.
Field.manpage: Overall reduction factor to apply, which will be used for X and Y even if a different factor is entered for Z.

Field.name: ZReductionFactor
Field.usage: Factor to reduce in Z dimension, default is overall factor
Field.tooltip: Factor to reduce by in Z; the default is to reduce the same in all dimensions. Can be non-integer.

Field.name: LowPassRadiusSigma
Field.usage: Radius and sigma for high-frequency Gaussian roll-off to 0.0
Field.tooltip: Cutoff radius and sigma for low pass filter to provide a high-frequency Gaussian filtering. Values are in reciprocal pixels as usual.
Field.manpage: Cutoff radius and sigma for a low pass filter that imposes a high-frequency Gaussian roll-off to 0.0. This option cannot be entered with \fB-deconv\fR.

Field.name: DeconvolutionStrength
Field.tooltip: Strength of the deconvolution, which determines how much low frequencies are boosted (higher values boost more). Values of ~0.25-1.0 may be useful. Values have same meaning as in Warp; divide values used in IsoNet by 3.
Field.manpage: The option activates a deconvolution filter by specifying the overall strength of the deconvolution, which controls the degree to which low frequencies are boosted. Values around 0.25 to 1 may be useful. The bigger the value, the more low frequencies are accentuated. This value is treated as it is in Warp; values used in IsoNet need to be divided by 3 to have the same effect here. This option cannot be entered with \fB-lowpass\fR. ^ ^The following 7 entries are used for the deconvolution filter.

Field.name: SNRFalloff
Field.usage: Falloff rate in the assumed SNR with frequency (default 0.7)
Field.tooltip: Falloff rate of the assumed SNR with frequency; higher values attenuate high frequencies more. The default is 0.7.
Field.manpage: Falloff rate with frequency of the signal-to-noise ratio assumed for computing the deconvolution filter; higher values attenuate high frequencies more. Some users suggest keeping this value comparable to the \fB-deconv\fR entry. The default is 0.7, the value in IsoNet.

Field.name: HighPassNyquist
Field.usage: Cutoff for high-pass filter as fraction of Nyquist (default 0.02)
Field.tooltip: Cutoff frequency of a high-pass filter to prevent excessive boosting of the lowest frequencies. The value is expressed as a fraction of Nyquist; the default is 0.02, which is 0.01/pixel.
Field.manpage: Cutoff frequency of a high-pass filter to prevent excessive boosting of the lowest frequencies, where the CTF is low. For consistency with Warp and IsoNet, the value is expressed as the fraction of Nyquist, and is thus twice the usual frequency in reciprocal pixels. The default is 0.02 as in IsoNet.

Field.name: PixelSize
Field.usage: Pixel size in nanometers, overrides the pixel spacing in the file header
Field.manpage: Pixel size in nanometers. This entry is needed only if the pixel size in the image file header is incorrect, but the program will try to determine is value by getting the raw stack pixel size in the Ctfplotter(1) command file and comparing pixel sizes in the raw stack and input volume headers.

Field.name: Voltage
Field.manpage: Microscope voltage in kV; the default is 300. The program will try to determine this value from the Ctfplotter(1) command file.

Field.name: SphericalAberration
Field.manpage: Spherical aberration (Cs) in mm; the default is 2.7. The program will try to determine this value from the Ctfplotter(1) command file.

Field.name: DefocusInMicrons
Field.tooltip: The defocus in microns (underfocus positive). This entry is not needed if Ctfplotter was run successfully; the program will try to get the defocus from the lowest tilt view of the ".defocus" file. Other microscope parameters (Cs and voltage) are taken from ctfplotter.com.
Field.manpage: The defocus in microns (underfocus positive). The program will try to determine this from the lowest tilt view of the ".defocus" file output by Ctfplotter(1). If that is not possible, the value must be entered.

Field.name: PhaseShift
Field.tooltip: Phase shift in degrees. This entry is needed if you want to account for a phase shift; the program does not take it from the ".defocus" file.

Field.name: ModeToOutput
Field.usage: Mode for output: 0 for byte, 1 or 6 for integer, 2 or 12 for float
Field.tooltip: The storage mode of the output from both reduction and filtering; 0 for byte, 1 for 16-bit signed integer, 6 for 16-bit unsigned integer, 2 for 32-bit floating point, or 12 for 16-bit floating point. The default is the mode of the input file. With the deconvolution filter, byte files may need to be changed to mode 1.
Field.manpage: The storage mode of the output file from either Binvol(1) or Mtffilter(1); 0 for byte, 1 for 16-bit signed integer, 6 for 16-bit unsigned integer, 2 for 32-bit floating point, or 12 for 16-bit floating point. The default is the mode of the input file. See the Mtffilter(1) man page for some details about mode 12.

Field.name: SetupChunksIfMemoryError
Field.usage: If Mtffilter has insufficient memory, run Chunksetup for running in parallel
Field.manpage: If Mtffilter(1) exits with an error indicating that the memory needed is bigger than the allowed amount, or that memory for the image array could not be allocated, then run Chunksetup(1) to create command files for processing the volume in parallel.
